Dynamic coronary artery obstruction: in some cases, unstable angina may occur due to dynamic obstruction of the coronary arteries, such as coronary artery spasm (variant angina) or microvascular dysfunction.
Inflammation: inflammation within the coronary arteries can contribute to plaque instability and trigger episodes of unstable angina.

qs.q: Which of the following imaging modalities can directly visualize coronary arteries to identify blockages and guide treatment decisions?
qs.e: Coronary angiography visualizes the coronary arteries to identify blockages and guide treatment decisions. Chest X-rays and echocardiography assess overall structure, function, and complications like pulmonary edema, but do not directly image coronary lumens as clearly.

qs.q: A 70-year-old woman with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis experiences episodes of exertional chest pain despite normal coronary arteries on angiography. What is the primary pathophysiological driver of her angina?
o: Episodic coronary vasospasm triggered by left atrial stretch receptors
Severe systemic hypotension causing inadequate cerebral and coronary blood flow
Primary pulmonary hypertension reducing overall systemic arterial saturation
Increased myocardial oxygen demand coupled with reduced subendocardial perfusion
qs.e: Left ventricular hypertrophy and high intramyocardial wall tension account for increased oxygen demands, which, along with decreased diastolic coronary blood flow via elevated LVEDP, cause angina. It occurs independently of obstructive coronary atherosclerosis.

qs.q: A 60-year-old woman with chronic left ventricular volume overload from a leaking aortic valve develops angina despite normal coronary arteries. Which pathophysiological combination best explains her myocardial ischemia?
o: Reduced ventricular mass lowers overall oxygen use and prevents ischemia.
Systemic hypertension increases coronary perfusion and lowers end-diastolic volume.
Elevated coronary resistance matches the reduced myocardial demand.
Decreased diastolic pressure reduces perfusion while enlarged ventricle raises demand.
qs.e: Aortic regurgitation lowers diastolic perfusion pressure while ventricular dilation increases wall stress and oxygen demand. Reduced ventricular mass is incorrect because volume overload causes hypertrophy and increased mass, further raising oxygen demand.

qs.q: Which imaging technique uses contrast dye and X-rays to visualize coronary arteries and identify blockages?
qs.e: ** Coronary angiography is an invasive imaging technique that uses contrast dye and X-rays to directly visualize the coronary arteries and identify blockages or narrowing.

ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The coronary arteries arise from the aortic sinuses and supply the heart muscle. Their course, branches, and relationships determine perfusion and vulnerability to disease.

sections.p: The coronary arteries are the main blood supply to the myocardium, branching from the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve. Their distribution ensures oxygenated blood reaches all cardiac layers.
b: Right coronary artery (RCA) supplies right atrium, right ventricle, SA node, AV node; Left coronary artery (LCA) supplies left ventricle and left atrium.

sections.p: Both arteries originate from the aortic root: the RCA from the right coronary cusp and the LCA from the left coronary cusp. The LCA divides into the left anterior descending (LAD) and circumflex (LCx).
b: RCA runs in the right atrioventricular groove; LCA in the left atrioventricular groove.

sections.p: The coronary arteries lie in the atrioventricular grooves, adjacent to the great cardiac veins. The RCA is close to the right atrium and right ventricle, while the LCx runs near the left atrium.
b: The LAD runs anteriorly over the interventricular septum; the LCx courses posteriorly along the left atrioventricular groove.

sections.p: They deliver oxygenated blood to the myocardium. Branches such as the marginal, septal, and obtuse marginal arteries supply specific myocardial regions.
b: Coronary perfusion occurs mainly during diastole, when aortic pressure exceeds myocardial pressure.

sections.p: Autonomic innervation modulates coronary tone. Sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate and vasoconstriction; parasympathetic activity promotes vasodilation.
b: Vagal afferents from the heart influence coronary flow via baroreceptor reflexes.

sections.p: Beyond oxygen delivery, coronary arteries regulate myocardial metabolism, support electrical conduction, and respond to ischemic stimuli by vasodilation.
b: Coronary autoregulation maintains constant flow despite changes in perfusion pressure.

sections.p: Atherosclerotic plaques, thrombosis, or emboli can occlude coronary arteries, leading to myocardial infarction. Coronary anomalies may cause sudden death.
b: Coronary artery disease is the leading cause of death worldwide.

sections.p: Remember the mnemonic "RCA supplies right, LCA supplies left" and that the LAD is the "widowmaker" due to its critical territory.
b: In acute MI, ST elevation in leads V1–V4 suggests LAD occlusion.

whenToSeekHelp: Chest pain with pressure or burning, especially if radiating to arm or jaw; shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, or syncope.
